description: Transform the Bitcoinvestments cryptocurrency education and investment platform from its current ~92% complete state into a fully enterprise-grade, professional, production-ready SaaS product. The platform is built with React 18 + TypeScript on Vite, Supabase (PostgreSQL + Auth), Cloudflare Workers/Pages, Stripe payments, and Web3 integrations (RainbowKit, SIWE, wagmi/viem). It currently has 98+ components, 90+ services, 50+ pages, and 37 database migrations. This PRD covers all remaining gaps: code quality, testing, security hardening, performance optimization, monitoring/observability, CI/CD, API documentation, accessibility, SEO, and enterprise features needed to achieve production readiness.

userStories.title: Add Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system
userStories.description: Implement a comprehensive RBAC system with defined roles (user, premium, advisor, admin, super_admin), permissions, and a permission checking utility that integrates with the existing auth system.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/rbac.ts created with Role enum, Permission enum, and role-permission mapping
Roles defined: user (free), premium (subscriber), advisor (business plan), admin, super_admin
Permissions defined for: portfolio (read/write/share), blog (read/create/edit/delete/publish), forum (read/post/moderate), admin (users/subscriptions/analytics/content), api (read/write)
usePermission() hook created that checks current user's role against required permission
ProtectedRoute component updated to accept required permissions (not just auth check)
Admin routes restricted to admin/super_admin roles
Advisor routes restricted to advisor role and above
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Current system has basic role check (user.is_admin). This story formalizes it into a proper RBAC. Keep backward compatible with existing AdminRoute component.

userStories.title: Add comprehensive audit logging for admin actions
userStories.description: Implement an audit logging system that records all admin actions (user management, content moderation, subscription changes, system configuration) with timestamps, actor, action, and affected resources.
acceptanceCriteria: Supabase migration adds audit_logs table: id, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, details (JSONB), ip_address, timestamp
src/services/auditLog.ts created with logAction() function
Admin user management actions logged (ban, unban, role change, delete)
Content moderation actions logged (approve, reject, flag, delete)
Subscription override actions logged
Admin analytics page shows filterable audit log table
Audit logs are append-only (no UPDATE or DELETE allowed via RLS)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Audit logs must be immutable. RLS policy should allow INSERT for admins and SELECT for super_admins only. Regular admins can see their own audit entries.

userStories.title: Add data export and GDPR compliance tools
userStories.description: Implement user data export (download all my data) and account deletion functionality to comply with GDPR/CCPA requirements. Add privacy controls to user profile settings.
acceptanceCriteria: Profile settings page has 'Download My Data' button that exports all user data as JSON
Export includes: profile, portfolios, holdings, transactions, alerts, forum posts, settings
Profile settings has 'Delete My Account' with confirmation flow requiring password re-entry
Account deletion soft-deletes user data (30-day recovery window) then hard-deletes
Deletion cascades properly to all related tables (holdings, transactions, posts, etc.)
Email notification sent on data export and deletion request
Privacy policy page updated to reference data export and deletion rights
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure) and Article 20 (Right to Data Portability). Stripe customer data must be handled separately via Stripe API. Don't delete audit logs.

userStories.title: Add Web Vitals monitoring and performance dashboard
userStories.description: Implement Core Web Vitals tracking (LCP, FID, CLS, TTFB, INP) using the existing useWebVitals hook, report metrics to an analytics endpoint, and create an admin performance dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: useWebVitals hook enhanced to report LCP, FID/INP, CLS, TTFB, FCP metrics
Metrics sent to /api/log-performance endpoint (new) in batches
Performance data stored in Supabase table: web_vitals (page, metric, value, timestamp, user_agent, connection_type)
Admin dashboard page /admin/performance shows: p50/p75/p95 for each metric, trend charts over time, breakdown by page route, breakdown by device type
Performance budgets defined: LCP < 2.5s, FID < 100ms, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms
Alerts triggered when p75 exceeds budget thresholds
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Existing useWebVitals hook is in src/hooks/. Use web-vitals library for standardized metric collection. Report in batches to avoid excessive API calls.

userStories.title: Add environment configuration management
userStories.description: Create a typed environment configuration system that validates all required environment variables at startup, provides defaults for optional ones, and fails fast with clear error messages for missing required vars.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/env.ts created with Zod schema validating all VITE_ environment variables
Schema defines which vars are required vs optional with defaults
Application fails fast on startup with clear message if required vars are missing
Type-safe access: env.SUPABASE_URL instead of import.meta.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL
functions/api/_shared/env.ts created for Cloudflare Worker environment validation
Worker env validates: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, RESEND_API_KEY at request time
.env.example file updated with all variables and descriptions
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Vite exposes VITE_ prefixed vars via import.meta.env. Cloudflare Workers receive env as function parameter. Both need validation but with different mechanisms.

userStories.title: Add database connection pooling and query optimization
userStories.description: Optimize Supabase client configuration with connection pooling, add query performance monitoring, and optimize the most frequently called queries with proper indexing recommendations.
acceptanceCriteria: Supabase client configured with proper connection settings (persistSession, autoRefreshToken, detectSessionInUrl)
Database queries in top 5 most-called services optimized with select() column filtering (no SELECT *)
Supabase migration adds indexes for: holdings(portfolio_id), transactions(portfolio_id, created_at), price_alerts(user_id, is_active), articles(slug, published), forum_posts(created_at, is_published)
Query performance baseline documented for key operations
React Query configured with proper staleTime (5min) and cacheTime (30min) for each query type
Unnecessary re-fetches eliminated via proper query key management
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Supabase uses PostgREST which handles connection pooling at the infrastructure level. Focus on query optimization and React Query cache configuration.

userStories.title: Add data backup and recovery documentation
userStories.description: Document the database backup strategy, create backup verification scripts, and add a disaster recovery runbook for the production Supabase instance.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/BACKUP_AND_RECOVERY.md created with: automated backup schedule (Supabase built-in daily backups), manual backup procedure using pg_dump, point-in-time recovery steps, data restoration procedure
Script tools/backup-verify.sh created that tests backup connectivity and basic restore to a test database
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) defined and documented
Runbook includes: incident response steps, communication templates, escalation contacts
Stripe data recovery documented (separate from database)
Cloudflare KV data recovery documented
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Supabase Pro plan includes daily automated backups with 7-day retention. Document how to access these and supplement with custom backup scripts.

userStories.title: Add comprehensive README and developer onboarding guide
userStories.description: Create a professional README.md with project overview, architecture diagram, setup instructions, development workflow, and contribution guidelines. Create a separate CONTRIBUTING.md.
acceptanceCriteria: README.md includes: project description, key features list, architecture overview (frontend/backend/database/infra), tech stack badges, prerequisites (Node 20+, npm), quick start (clone, install, configure env, run), available npm scripts, project structure overview, deployment instructions
CONTRIBUTING.md includes: branch naming conventions, commit message format, PR template, code style guide, testing requirements
Architecture diagram shows: React SPA → Cloudflare Pages → API Functions → Supabase + External APIs
Environment setup clearly lists all required and optional env vars
Common issues and troubleshooting section included
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Current README may exist but is likely outdated. The docs/ folder has 31 files but no consolidated getting-started guide. This should be the single entry point for new developers.

userStories.title: Add feature flags system for gradual rollouts
userStories.description: Implement a simple feature flags system using Supabase that allows enabling/disabling features per user, per role, or globally without code deployments.
acceptanceCriteria: Supabase migration adds feature_flags table: id, flag_key, description, enabled_globally, enabled_roles (text[]), enabled_users (uuid[]), created_at, updated_at
src/services/featureFlags.ts created with: isFeatureEnabled(flagKey, userId?, role?) function
useFeatureFlag(flagKey) React hook created for conditional rendering
Admin page /admin/feature-flags for managing flags (toggle, set roles, set users)
Feature flags cached client-side with 5-minute TTL to reduce database calls
At least 3 existing features wrapped in feature flags (e.g., web3Features, socialTrading, aiAssistant)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Keep this simple - no need for a full feature flag service like LaunchDarkly. A Supabase table + React hook is sufficient for this scale.

userStories.title: Add rate limit dashboard and abuse detection
userStories.description: Create an admin dashboard showing API rate limit usage, blocked requests, and potential abuse patterns. Add automated alerting for sustained rate limit violations.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin page /admin/rate-limits shows: requests per endpoint over time, top rate-limited IPs, blocked request count by endpoint, abuse pattern detection (sustained 429s from same IP)
Rate limit data aggregated from Cloudflare KV store into Supabase for historical analysis
Automated alert (email to admin) when an IP exceeds rate limits 50+ times in 1 hour
IP block list management: admin can manually block/unblock IPs
Dashboard shows real-time rate limit status for each endpoint category
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Rate limit data is in RATE_LIMIT_KV. Need a scheduled worker or API endpoint to aggregate this data. Keep the UI simple and focused on actionable insights.

userStories.title: Add email template system for transactional emails
userStories.description: Create a templated email system with responsive HTML email templates for all transactional emails (welcome, password reset, price alerts, newsletter, subscription confirmations).
acceptanceCriteria: src/email-templates/ directory created with HTML template files
Templates created for: welcome, password-reset, price-alert, subscription-confirmed, subscription-cancelled, weekly-newsletter, data-export-ready, account-deletion-warning
All templates are responsive (mobile-friendly) using inline CSS
Templates use a consistent brand design (logo, colors, footer with unsubscribe link)
Template rendering function accepts data object and returns HTML string
Unsubscribe link included in all marketing emails (CAN-SPAM compliance)
Templates tested with Litmus or Email on Acid for cross-client rendering
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Resend API and AWS SES are already configured for sending. Focus on the template HTML. Email HTML is notoriously tricky - use tables for layout, inline styles, and test in major clients.

userStories.title: Add multi-tenant data isolation for business plans
userStories.description: Implement data isolation between business plan organizations (Advisor and Enterprise tiers) so that each organization's data is completely segregated with organization-level admin controls.
acceptanceCriteria: Supabase migration adds organizations table: id, name, plan_tier, owner_id, created_at
Supabase migration adds organization_members table: org_id, user_id, role (owner, admin, member), invited_at, joined_at
RLS policies updated so organization members only see their org's data
Organization admin can: invite/remove members, view org-wide portfolio analytics, manage billing
Data queries automatically scoped to user's organization when applicable
Free/premium users unaffected (null organization_id)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Business plans: Advisor ($49/mo) and Enterprise ($99/mo). Multi-tenancy is essential for enterprise. Use RLS policies with organization_id for data isolation.

userStories.title: Add API key management for developer portal
userStories.description: Enhance the existing developer portal with proper API key lifecycle management including key generation, rotation, revocation, usage tracking, and quota enforcement per API tier.
acceptanceCriteria: Developer portal page shows all active API keys with creation date and last used timestamp
Generate new API key with name/description (key shown once, then hashed)
Revoke API key with confirmation dialog
Rotate API key (generates new, optionally keeps old active for grace period)
Usage dashboard shows: requests today, requests this month, quota remaining, rate limit status
API keys enforce tier limits: Starter (10K req/mo), Professional (100K req/mo)
Email notification when usage reaches 80% and 100% of quota
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: api_access table already exists in database. API tiers already defined: Starter ($29/mo monthly, $290/yr yearly), Professional ($79/mo monthly, $790/yr yearly).

userStories.title: Add comprehensive error pages (404, 500, 403, maintenance)
userStories.description: Create polished, branded error pages for all HTTP error states with helpful messaging, navigation options, and error reporting. Include a maintenance mode page.
acceptanceCriteria: 404 page redesigned with: search bar, suggested popular pages, 'Go Home' button, animation/illustration
500 page created with: friendly error message, error ID for support reference, 'Try Again' button, link to status page
403 page created with: 'Access Denied' message, login prompt if unauthenticated, upgrade prompt if subscription-gated
Maintenance mode page created with: estimated return time, email signup for notification, social media links
Feature flag controls maintenance mode (from US-044 or environment variable)
All error pages match the existing design system
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Current 404 page exists but may need polish. 500 and 403 pages likely don't exist. Maintenance mode can be triggered via feature flag or MAINTENANCE_MODE env var.

userStories.title: Add end-to-end encryption for sensitive user data
userStories.description: Implement client-side encryption for sensitive user data (API keys, wallet private notes, personal financial data) before storing in Supabase, with decryption only on the user's device.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/encryption.ts created using Web Crypto API (AES-256-GCM)
Encryption key derived from user's password via PBKDF2 (100K iterations, SHA-256)
Encrypted fields: API keys stored by user, wallet notes/labels, custom portfolio notes with financial details
Encryption/decryption happens client-side only - server never sees plaintext
Key derivation cached in memory (sessionStorage) for session duration
User prompted to enter password for decryption if session expired
Clear documentation that password reset will make encrypted data unrecoverable (or implement key escrow)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use SubtleCrypto API available in all modern browsers. AES-256-GCM provides both encryption and authentication. This is for additional data protection, not replacing HTTPS/TLS.

userStories.title: Add webhook system for external integrations
userStories.description: Build a webhook delivery system that allows enterprise users to receive real-time notifications for events (price alerts triggered, portfolio changes, subscription events) via HTTP callbacks.
acceptanceCriteria: Supabase migration adds webhook_endpoints table: id, user_id, url, secret, events (text[]), is_active, created_at
Supabase migration adds webhook_deliveries table: id, endpoint_id, event, payload, status, attempts, response_code, delivered_at
Developer portal has webhook management UI: add endpoint URL, select events, view delivery history
Webhook payloads signed with HMAC-SHA256 using endpoint secret
Failed deliveries retried 3 times with exponential backoff (1min, 5min, 30min)
Webhook events: price_alert.triggered, portfolio.updated, subscription.changed
Delivery history shows last 100 deliveries with status and response
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Enterprise feature. Use HMAC-SHA256 for webhook signatures (same pattern as Stripe webhooks). Delivery via Cloudflare Worker scheduled or triggered by database changes.

userStories.title: Add internationalization (i18n) infrastructure
userStories.description: Set up the i18n infrastructure using react-i18next so the platform can be translated into multiple languages. Extract all user-facing strings from core pages into translation files.
acceptanceCriteria: react-i18next and i18next installed and configured
src/i18n/ directory created with: config.ts, locales/en.json as default locale
Translation namespace structure: common, auth, dashboard, portfolio, pricing, errors
At least the following pages fully extracted to translation keys: Home, Login, Signup, Pricing, Dashboard
useTranslation() hook used in extracted components
Language selector component created (hidden until more languages are added)
Locale detection from browser preferences implemented
Pluralization and interpolation patterns documented for translators
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Start with English extraction only - actual translations come later. The infrastructure is what matters for enterprise readiness. Use namespaced translation keys.

userStories.title: Add comprehensive admin analytics dashboard
userStories.description: Enhance the admin analytics page with key business metrics: MRR, churn rate, user growth, feature adoption, conversion funnels, and cohort analysis.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin analytics shows: MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue) from Stripe, active subscriber count by tier, churn rate (monthly), new user signups over time (daily/weekly/monthly chart)
Feature adoption metrics: % users using portfolio tracker, % using price alerts, % using Web3 features, % using forum
Conversion funnel: visitor → signup → free user → premium subscriber with drop-off rates
Revenue per user segment (free, premium, advisor, enterprise)
Data exportable as CSV
Dashboard loads within 3 seconds
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: MRR data may need to come from Stripe API or be calculated from subscription records in Supabase. Use Chart.js (already installed) for visualizations.

userStories.title: Add automated newsletter content generation pipeline
userStories.description: Enhance the weekly newsletter automation with content curation from blog posts, price movements, and platform updates. Create newsletter preview and approval workflow for admins.
acceptanceCriteria: Newsletter worker automatically curates: top 3 blog posts of the week, notable price movements (>10% change), new platform features, upcoming webinars/events
Admin page /admin/newsletter shows preview of next newsletter before sending
Admin can edit, approve, or reject the auto-generated newsletter
Newsletter includes personalized elements: user's portfolio performance summary (opt-in), relevant price alerts
Unsubscribe link works correctly and immediately removes from list
Newsletter metrics tracked: open rate, click-through rate, unsubscribe rate
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Newsletter worker is in workers/weekly-newsletter-cron.ts, deployed via wrangler-newsletter.toml. Resend API handles sending. Enhance the content generation logic.

userStories.title: Add SSL certificate pinning and API security hardening
userStories.description: Implement additional API security measures including request signing for sensitive endpoints, API key hashing with bcrypt, and certificate transparency monitoring.
acceptanceCriteria: API keys stored as bcrypt hashes in database, never plaintext
Sensitive mutation endpoints require request timestamp (within 5-minute window) to prevent replay attacks
All Cloudflare Worker responses include: X-Request-Id header, X-Response-Time header
Request body size limits enforced: 1MB for standard endpoints, 10MB for file uploads
SQL injection prevention verified: all Supabase queries use parameterized inputs (audit existing code)
Documented security checklist in docs/SECURITY_CHECKLIST.md covering OWASP Top 10
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Cloudflare handles SSL/TLS termination. Focus on application-layer security. API key hashing is critical - current implementation may store keys in plaintext.

userStories.title: Add load testing configuration and performance baselines
userStories.description: Create load testing scripts using k6 or Artillery that simulate realistic traffic patterns and establish performance baselines for key API endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: Load test configuration created in tools/load-tests/ directory
Test scenarios: normal load (100 concurrent users), peak load (500 concurrent users), price alert spike (1000 alerts triggered simultaneously)
Key endpoints tested: /api/health, /api/v1/market/prices, /api/coingecko/*, /api/check-price-alerts
Performance baselines documented: p50, p95, p99 response times, error rates, throughput (req/sec)
Test results stored in test-reports/load-tests/ for comparison
package.json has 'test:load' script
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: k6 is recommended for its JavaScript-native test scripts. Load tests should target a staging environment, never production without explicit approval.

userStories.title: Add Storybook for component documentation
userStories.description: Set up Storybook for the UI component library. Document all reusable UI components (buttons, inputs, cards, modals, skeletons) with interactive examples, props documentation, and visual regression baselines.
acceptanceCriteria: @storybook/react-vite installed and configured
Stories created for core UI components: Button, Input, Card, Modal, Skeleton, Toast, Badge, Alert, Dropdown
Each story shows all variants/states (default, hover, disabled, loading, error)
Props documented with argTypes and descriptions
Storybook builds without errors via 'npm run storybook:build'
package.json has 'storybook' and 'storybook:build' scripts
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Use @storybook/react-vite for native Vite integration. Focus on reusable UI primitives, not page-level components. This becomes the design system documentation.

userStories.title: Add real-time WebSocket notifications
userStories.description: Implement real-time notifications using Supabase Realtime subscriptions for live portfolio value updates, price alert triggers, and admin notifications.
acceptanceCriteria: src/services/realtime.ts created with Supabase Realtime subscription management
Dashboard receives live price updates without manual refresh
Price alert triggers push a real-time notification to the user's browser
Admin dashboard receives real-time new user signup notifications
Notification bell icon in header shows unread notification count with badge
Clicking notification bell shows dropdown with recent notifications
Notifications persisted in Supabase notifications table for history
WebSocket connection gracefully reconnects on disconnection
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Supabase Realtime is already available via @supabase/supabase-js. Use postgres_changes for table change subscriptions. Handle reconnection gracefully.

userStories.title: Add SSO/OAuth provider integration
userStories.description: Add social login options (Google, GitHub) and prepare SSO/SAML infrastructure for enterprise customers using Supabase Auth's built-in OAuth support.
acceptanceCriteria: Google OAuth login configured in Supabase Auth settings
GitHub OAuth login configured in Supabase Auth settings
Login page shows 'Continue with Google' and 'Continue with GitHub' buttons
OAuth flow properly creates/links user profile in users table
Existing email users can link OAuth accounts from profile settings
SSO/SAML configuration documented for enterprise customers (Supabase Enterprise feature)
OAuth users can still enable 2FA on their accounts
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Supabase Auth supports OAuth out of the box. Google and GitHub are the most common. SAML is a Supabase Enterprise feature - document the path but don't implement.

userStories.title: Final production readiness review and launch checklist
userStories.description: Create and execute a comprehensive production readiness checklist that validates all enterprise requirements are met: security, performance, monitoring, documentation, and compliance.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS_CHECKLIST.md created covering all categories
Security: CSP headers verified, rate limiting tested, input sanitization audited, OWASP Top 10 checked
Performance: Lighthouse score >90 for Performance, >90 for Accessibility, >90 for Best Practices, >90 for SEO
Monitoring: Sentry configured, health checks responding, logging operational
Testing: Unit test coverage >70% for core services, E2E tests passing for critical flows
Documentation: README complete, API docs complete, deployment guide verified
Compliance: GDPR data export works, CAN-SPAM unsubscribe works, Terms of Service and Privacy Policy links functional
All previous user stories verified as passing
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is the capstone story. Run through every checklist item and verify. Document any known issues or tech debt that should be addressed post-launch.

userStories.title: Add user onboarding wizard for first-time users
userStories.description: Create a guided onboarding flow that walks new users through key platform features after signup: setting up a portfolio, exploring the dashboard, configuring price alerts, and discovering educational content.
acceptanceCriteria: Onboarding wizard triggers automatically after first login (tracked via user metadata flag)
Step 1: Welcome screen with overview of platform capabilities
Step 2: Create your first portfolio with guided prompts
Step 3: Tour of the dashboard with highlighted key features (prices, Fear & Greed, news)
Step 4: Set up your first price alert
Step 5: Discover learning resources with recommendations based on experience level
Users can skip onboarding at any step and access it later from profile settings
Onboarding completion tracked in analytics (funnel drop-off per step)
Responsive design works on mobile and desktop
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Onboarding is critical for new user retention. Users who complete onboarding are significantly more likely to become paying subscribers. Track each step completion as an analytics event.

userStories.title: Add global search functionality across the platform
userStories.description: Implement a comprehensive search feature accessible from the header that searches across blog posts, glossary terms, educational guides, exchanges, wallets, scam reports, and calculator tools.
acceptanceCriteria: Search input in the header with Cmd/Ctrl+K keyboard shortcut to open
Search modal/dropdown with categorized results (Articles, Glossary, Guides, Tools, Exchanges)
Results include: title, description preview, category badge, and direct link
Debounced search (300ms) to reduce unnecessary queries
Recent searches stored in localStorage for quick access
Empty state shows popular searches and trending topics
SearchResults page updated to use the same search backend
Search queries logged for analytics (what users are looking for)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The SearchResults page exists but search is basic. A Cmd+K modal is the modern standard for SaaS platforms. Client-side search via a pre-built index (lunr.js or fuse.js) may be sufficient given the static content.

userStories.title: Add user referral program with tracking and rewards
userStories.description: Implement a referral program that gives existing users a unique referral link. When someone signs up via the link and subscribes, both the referrer and the new user receive a reward (e.g., 1 month free on premium).
acceptanceCriteria: Each user has a unique referral code accessible from their profile page
Referral link format: https://bitcoinvestments.net/signup?ref=CODE
Referral tracking: store referrer_id on signup in the users table
Supabase migration adds referrals table: id, referrer_id, referred_id, status (pending/converted/rewarded), created_at, converted_at
Referral converts when the referred user subscribes to any paid plan
Reward: 1 month free extension on current plan for referrer (applied as Stripe coupon)
Referral stats displayed on profile: total referrals, conversions, rewards earned
Email notification sent to referrer when their referral converts
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Referral programs are the cheapest user acquisition channel. The affiliate system already handles partner referrals - this is for user-to-user referrals. Use Stripe coupons for reward fulfillment.

userStories.title: Add mobile-responsive audit and fix critical breakpoints
userStories.description: Conduct a systematic audit of all major pages on mobile viewports (320px, 375px, 414px) and fix layout issues, overflow problems, touch target sizes, and navigation usability on mobile devices.
acceptanceCriteria: All pages render without horizontal overflow on 320px viewport
Touch targets (buttons, links) meet minimum 44x44px requirement
Mobile navigation menu works correctly with all items accessible
Tables on Dashboard, Admin, and Compare pages are horizontally scrollable or use card layout on mobile
Calculator forms are usable on mobile with proper input types (numeric keyboard for numbers)
Chart components are responsive and readable on mobile
Modal dialogs don't extend beyond viewport on mobile
Font sizes readable without zooming (minimum 16px for body text on mobile)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Over 60% of crypto users access platforms on mobile. Tailwind's responsive utilities should handle most cases, but data-heavy pages (tables, charts) often need explicit mobile layouts.

userStories.title: Add dark/light mode toggle with system preference detection
userStories.description: Implement a dark/light mode toggle that persists the user's preference in localStorage and defaults to their system preference. Currently the platform is dark-mode only.
acceptanceCriteria: Theme toggle button added to the header navigation (sun/moon icon)
Light mode theme defined with appropriate colors for all components
Theme preference stored in localStorage and respected on page load
System preference (prefers-color-scheme) detected as default when no explicit choice is set
Tailwind dark: variant classes used consistently across all components
No flash of wrong theme on page load (theme applied before first render)
All text meets WCAG 4.5:1 contrast ratio in both modes
Charts and data visualizations readable in both modes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Currently dark-mode only. Many users prefer light mode, especially during daytime. Use Tailwind's dark mode class strategy. Apply theme class to <html> element before React hydrates to prevent flash.

userStories.title: Add notification preferences center for users
userStories.description: Create a notification preferences page in user profile settings where users can control which notifications they receive (email, push, in-app) for different event categories.
acceptanceCriteria: Profile settings page has a 'Notification Preferences' section
Categories: Price alerts, Portfolio updates, Newsletter, Security alerts, Product updates, Community activity
Each category has toggles for: Email, In-App (future), Push (future)
Preferences stored in user_preferences table in Supabase
Email sending functions check preferences before sending non-essential emails
Security alerts (login from new device, password change) are always sent (cannot be disabled)
Changes save automatically (optimistic UI with toast confirmation)
Unsubscribe links in emails respect these preferences
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: CAN-SPAM requires unsubscribe links but allowing granular control improves user experience and reduces total unsubscribes. Security notifications should be mandatory.

userStories.title: Add two-factor authentication recovery codes
userStories.description: Generate and display one-time recovery codes when users enable 2FA, so they can regain access if they lose their authenticator device. Store hashed recovery codes in the database.
acceptanceCriteria: When 2FA is enabled, generate 10 one-time recovery codes
Recovery codes displayed once with option to download as text file or copy to clipboard
Recovery codes stored as bcrypt hashes in Supabase (never stored in plaintext after initial display)
Login flow accepts a recovery code as alternative to TOTP when 2FA is required
Each recovery code can only be used once (marked as used after successful auth)
User can regenerate recovery codes from profile settings (invalidates all previous codes)
Warning displayed when fewer than 3 unused recovery codes remain
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: 2FA recovery codes are critical for account recovery. Without them, users who lose their phone are permanently locked out. Store hashes, not plaintext. Use a distinct table: user_recovery_codes(id, user_id, code_hash, used, created_at).

userStories.title: Add user-facing account activity log
userStories.description: Show users a log of their own account activity including logins, password changes, 2FA changes, and sensitive actions. This builds trust and helps users detect unauthorized access.
acceptanceCriteria: Profile settings page has an 'Account Activity' section
Activity log shows: login events (with device/browser info and approximate location from IP), password changes, 2FA enable/disable, email changes, profile updates
Entries show timestamp, action description, device info, and IP-derived location (city/country level)
Pagination with last 50 activities shown by default
Suspicious activity highlighted (login from new device, login from unusual location)
Option to 'Sign out all other devices' if suspicious activity is detected
Activity data stored in user_activity_log table with 90-day retention
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is both a security feature and a trust signal. Users handling cryptocurrency assets want visibility into who accessed their account. Use IP geolocation (free MaxMind GeoLite2 database) for location.

userStories.title: Add smart API response caching layer to reduce CoinGecko calls
userStories.description: Implement an intelligent caching layer in the CoinGecko Cloudflare Worker proxy that uses Cloudflare KV with tiered TTLs based on data freshness requirements, reducing API calls by 80%+.
acceptanceCriteria: CoinGecko proxy worker uses Cloudflare KV (COINGECKO_CACHE_KV) for response caching
Cache TTL tiers: prices = 60s, market data = 5min, coin details = 1hr, historical data = 24hr
Stale-while-revalidate pattern: serve cached data while fetching fresh data in background
Cache key includes query parameters for proper isolation
Response headers include X-Cache-Status (HIT/MISS/STALE) for debugging
CoinGecko 429 rate limit responses trigger extended cache TTL (serve stale data for up to 30min)
Cache statistics endpoint for admin: total requests, hit rate, miss rate
Free tier users always get cached data (no real-time), premium users get fresher data
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: CoinGecko free tier allows 10-50 calls/min. With caching, we can serve thousands of users within this limit. The worker proxy already exists - this adds KV caching to it.

userStories.title: Add automated accessibility testing in CI pipeline
userStories.description: Integrate axe-core accessibility testing into the CI pipeline to automatically detect WCAG 2.1 AA violations on every pull request, preventing accessibility regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: @axe-core/playwright or @axe-core/react installed as devDependency
Playwright accessibility test suite created that runs axe-core on 10 key pages: Home, Dashboard, Login, Signup, Pricing, Learn, Glossary, Compare, Blog, Profile
Tests fail on any critical or serious accessibility violations
Moderate violations reported as warnings (don't fail build)
Test results output includes violation details with remediation suggestions
CI pipeline step added for accessibility testing
package.json has 'test:a11y' script
Baseline of current violations documented so regressions can be tracked
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Automated a11y testing catches ~30% of WCAG issues (color contrast, missing labels, ARIA misuse). Manual testing is still needed for keyboard navigation and screen reader flows.
